title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: The cubane {Ln4(μ3-OH)4} is the most common single building block; vertex-sharing cubanes produce Ln7, wheel-like Ln12 and Ln15, and cage-like Ln38 and Ln60, and the higher-nuclearity members of this series characteristically contain template anions whereas the lower-nuclearity ones do not.
explanation: Isolated cubanes supported by organic ligands are common. Two cubanes give two types of Ln8 or, by vertex-sharing, Ln7. When each cubane vertex-shares with two neighbors, wheels (Ln12, Ln15) and cages (Ln38, Ln60) result. The authors use this contrast to reinforce the role of anion templates in high-nuclearity assembly. Triangular {Ln3} assemblies up to Ln12 are likewise said to stay below nuclearity 20 when no template is present.
scope: Clusters whose cores are described as built only from cubanes or only from triangular {Ln3(μ3-OH)} units.
caveats: The nuclearity–template correlation is observational across the cited series, not a proof that a template is always required above a fixed nuclearity.
